newsitem.title: USA: Ex-girlfriend says she dumped Simpson by phone.
newsitem.headline: Ex-girlfriend says she dumped Simpson by phone.

text.p: O.J. Simpson's ex-girlfriend said on Wednesday that she broke off their romance by leaving a phone message for him on the day his former wife and her friend were murdered.

Testifying by videotape in Simpson's civil trial, model Paula Barbieri said she had then flown to Las Vegas and did not respond to several phone messages the ex-football star left on her machine on June 12, 1994.
Later that night, his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson was slashed to death along with Ronald Goldman.
Simpson was acquitted in a criminal trial last year of the two murders, but is now being sued by the victims' families for "wrongful death".

Asked about her split with Simpson, whom she had been dating again since April after breaking up with him the previous year, Barbieri testified that she had left him a message. "I think it was on his car phone," she said.

Barbieri said the breakup was a result of several things: "between work, the kids, golf and my schedule, it was just too difficult to work things out." At one point she said she only saw Simpson for about a week and a half between April and June 1994, because he was on the road or playing golf.

Asked what Simpson said in the messages he left for her after her early-morning call, Barbieri said: "Something about (how) we were talking the night before about filling the house with babies and (asking) what was wrong now."

From this response, Barbieri testified she understood he had received her message. The testimony was significant because Simpson testified earlier in the trial that he never received Barbieri's message on the day of the killings.

Speaking in a sometimes faltering voice, the elegant, red-haired model denied the two had had a fight the night before, but said she was upset with Simpson because she was still going through the "healing process" from their first breakup.
At his criminal trial, the prosecution theorised that Simpson snapped emotionally after Barbieri broke off their relationship.
On cross-examination by Simpson's attorneys, Barbieri said she had never seen signs of violence from Simpson.
Earlier on Wednesday a volunteer at a battered women's shelter testified that a woman named Nicole called her five days before Simpson's ex-wife was killed, fearing for her life.

Nancy Ney, who was answering hotline phone calls for Los Angeles' Sojourn House in June 1994, said she now believes the woman who complained that her ex-husband was stalking and threatening her was Nicole Brown Simpson.
"She said he (her unidentified ex-husband) told her a few different times that if he ever caught her with another man, he would kill her," she said.
Ney said the woman was about the same age as Nicole Brown Simpson, with two young children and with a "high-profile" ex- husband, to whom she had been married eight years.
She said the voice on the phone was consistent with Nicole Brown Simpson's voice on a tape of a call to police in 1993.
Ney, who was not allowed to testify during the criminal trial, told jurors that the woman named Nicole called the shelter because she was "frightened" of her ex-husband.
"Her ex-husband had been calling her on the phone and begging her to please come back to him," Ney said. "She said he had been stalking her."
Ney said the caller told her that her ex-husband would show up in restaurants where she was dining and would often be behind her when she looked in her car's rear-view mirror.
Defence attorneys earlier tried to block Ney from testifying, arguing that the woman caller was never positively identified as Nicole Brown Simpson.
On cross-examination by Simpson's attorney Robert Baker, Ney conceded that consistent with the shelter's policy, she never asked the woman for her last name.
